theory.intro: When a problem mixes grams, kilograms and tonnes, first convert everything to one unit, then add, subtract or compare.
facts: Choose **one** common unit before calculating — usually the smallest in the problem.
Convert the answer back to a sensible unit at the end if needed.
steps: Pick a common unit for all the masses.
Convert each mass to that unit.
Add, subtract or compare, then state the answer clearly.

foundation.question_text: Find the total mass of $600\text{ g}$ and $1.4\text{ kg}$. Give the answer in kilograms.
A $3\text{ kg}$ bag has $850\text{ g}$ removed. What mass remains?
Which is heavier: $1250\text{ g}$ or $1.3\text{ kg}$, and by how much?
foundation.solution_text:
$1.3\text{ kg}=1300\text{ g}$
$1300-1250$
$=50\text{ g}$
$1.3\text{ kg}$ is heavier by $50\text{ g}$.

foundation.question_text: Three parcels have masses $250\text{ g}$, $750\text{ g}$ and $2\text{ kg}$. Find their total mass.
foundation.solution_text:
$250\text{ g}+750\text{ g}=1000\text{ g}$
$=1\text{ kg}$
$1\text{ kg}+2\text{ kg}$
$=3\text{ kg}$

foundation.question_text: A crate holds $8$ packets, each of mass $250\text{ g}$. Find the total mass in kilograms.
A van can carry $1\text{ t}$. It is loaded with $620\text{ kg}$. How much capacity remains?

development.question_text: A recipe uses $1.2\text{ kg}$ of flour and $350\text{ g}$ of sugar. Find the combined mass in grams.
A parcel initially has mass $5.6\text{ kg}$. Packaging of mass $425\text{ g}$ is removed. Give the new mass in kilograms.
A pallet contains $12$ boxes of mass $15\text{ kg}$ each and a base of mass $35\text{ kg}$. Find the total mass in tonnes.
development.solution_text:
$12\times15\text{ kg}$
$=180\text{ kg}$
$180\text{ kg}+35\text{ kg}$
$=215\text{ kg}$
$=0.215\text{ t}$

development.question_text: A truck has a mass limit of $4.5\text{ t}$. Its current mass is $3820\text{ kg}$. Can another $750\text{ kg}$ load be added?
development.solution_text:
$4.5\text{ t}=4500\text{ kg}$
$3820\text{ kg}+750\text{ kg}$
$=4570\text{ kg}$
$4570>4500$, so the load cannot be added.

development.question_text: A $2\text{ kg}$ bag of rice is divided equally into $5$ containers. What mass is in each container in grams?
A market stall sold $3.25\text{ kg}$ of apples in the morning and $2750\text{ g}$ in the afternoon. How many kilograms were sold altogether?

mastery.question_text: A lift can carry $0.75\text{ t}$. Four people have masses $82\text{ kg}$, $74\text{ kg}$, $91\text{ kg}$ and $68\text{ kg}$, and their equipment has mass $460\text{ kg}$. Is the load within the limit?
mastery.solution_text:
$82+74+91+68$
$=315\text{ kg}$
$315\text{ kg}+460\text{ kg}$
$=775\text{ kg}$
$0.75\text{ t}=750\text{ kg}$
The load exceeds the limit by $25\text{ kg}$.

mastery.question_text: A grocer has $9.5\text{ kg}$ of nuts. After filling $18$ bags of $450\text{ g}$ each, how much remains?
mastery.solution_text:
$18\times450\text{ g}$
$=8100\text{ g}$
$=8.1\text{ kg}$
$9.5\text{ kg}-8.1\text{ kg}$
$=1.4\text{ kg}$

mastery.question_text: Two identical crates and a $140\text{ kg}$ pallet have a total mass of $0.86\text{ t}$. Find the mass of each crate.
mastery.solution_text:
$0.86\text{ t}=860\text{ kg}$
$860\text{ kg}-140\text{ kg}$
$=720\text{ kg}$
$720\div2\text{ kg}$
$=360\text{ kg}$
